questions.title: Can the Course Have Extra Dropping Spots?
questions.question: True or false? Some golf courses might let you drop your ball in a special spot, like a dropping zone, if your ball goes into a penalty area.

choices.text: Only if you ask the referee

questions.explanation: Some golf courses have local rules that let you drop your ball in a certain spot, called a dropping zone, if your ball goes in a penalty area.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place on the golf course, like a pond or stream, where special rules say what you do if your ball goes in.
A marked spot where you are allowed to drop your ball after it goes in a penalty area.
Special rules made just for a certain golf course.

questions.teachingTip: Show a scorecard or a sign from a golf course where local rules or dropping zones are written down, and ask the child to spot them.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think you can only use a dropping zone if there is a referee, but you can use it if the local rules say so.
Some might think every course has dropping zones, but only courses that say so in their local rules do.

questions.title: Knowing When Local Rules Offer Extra Options
questions.question: True or false? Local Rules at some golf courses can give you extra options for dropping in penalty areas, like using a special dropping zone.

choices.text: Only if you ask the referee
